summary:
The starting pitcher category is the day's biggest red flag — R1 and R2 both show SP cratering to 42% over the last 14 days (80-109) against a 50% season baseline, a full 7.8pt cold swing at n=189. R3's SP number, by contrast, has stabilized at 48% (90-99), still below season but nowhere near as broken. Trust R3 over R1/R2 when SP is the driving signal today. Meanwhile bullpen and trends are the stable anchors across all three ratings: trends sit at 57% (108-81) for every rating, and bullpen is riding a 4-game win streak across R1/R2/R3 at 53% (101-88). R1's hitting category is the standout with a 6-game win streak and 53% clip (101-88) — worth leaning into if R1 hitting picks show up tonight.

On the P/L side, R3 is the rating to trust right now. Its 14-day strong-play window is +9.0u (46-42, 52%) and 30-day is +14.0u (81-74, 52%), while R1 and R2 are bleeding — R1 -2.0u over 30 days, R2 -3.0u over both 14 and 30-day windows despite a solid season base of +26.0u. R3 also carries the best season strong-play mark at 55% (125-104, +34.0u). For category combos, trends+runs remains the top agreement play at 56.2% (194-151, n=345), with trends+sp still strong at 55.4% despite SP's cold streak — the combo work is insulating against SP's individual slump. Team-wise, lean hard into TBR (72%, strong 16-4 at 80%, +18.0u) and BOS (76%, strong 13-6, +7.0u) when the model likes them — both are printing money. LAD's strong-play record (10-2, 83%, +13.0u) is quietly elite too. Fade HOU strong plays outright — 2-6 (25%, -7.0u) is the worst signal on the board today.
